DS3 VR 2.0.1: DLSS fixes. DLAA now works on PCs where 2.0 missed most frames, and DLSS can no longer make the picture worse than off.

**Fixed**
- **DLSS and DLAA missed most frames on many PCs.** DLSS has to run on the game's 3D image at one exact moment each frame. With some graphics settings (for example Shade Quality above Low, the default on most PCs), DS3 draws several look-alike images, and 2.0 kept switching between them, so DLAA rarely ran and the upscaling modes got no motion data. The mod now picks the image the game actually goes on to use, however many look-alikes there are.
- **A DLSS miss made the picture worse than DLSS off.** The camera jitter and texture sharpening DLSS needs stayed on even on frames DLSS did not process, which shimmered and aliased. They now switch off whenever DLSS is not doing its job, so the worst case looks like DLSS off.
- **Upscaling defaults:** the DLSS pairing (Previous frame) and halves (swapped) defaults now match geo-11's stereo image, so the upscaling modes get the right eye's depth and motion.

**Changed**
- **The installer sets Shade Quality to Low.** Higher settings can cause a twitchy effect in VR on some headsets. DLSS now works either way, so if you raise it, test it on your own headset. Updating does not change your setting.
- **The DLSS Status line shows how often DLSS is really working**, e.g. "DLAA working on 99% of frames", instead of just "running".
- **The upscaling modes (Quality to Ultra Perf) are marked experimental.** Because geo-11 makes the stereo image, DLSS upscales the finished picture, after the game's effects, so they look softer than DLSS does in a normal game. DLAA does not have this limit and is the recommended DLSS setting.
- The Graphics tab has a note about the game settings that matter in VR.
- **DLSS fine-tuning:** the Developer tab's DLSS settings (jitter and eye directions; for upscaling also pairing, halves and texture mip bias) can be tuned per headset and PC, since no single setting suits every setup. A new "DLSS settings to defaults" button, and Reset to defaults, put them back.

**Tip:** on mid-range RTX cards, the CNN DLSS model (the default) costs about half as much as Transformer.

**Updating from 2.0.0 or 1.0.x:** extract the new zip into the `Game` folder and overwrite the old files. You do not need to run `install-ds3vr.bat` again. Your settings are kept.

**New install:** extract `DS3VR-2.0.1.zip` into the game's `Game` folder (the one with `DarkSoulsIII.exe`), run `install-ds3vr.bat`, start your VR runtime, then launch Dark Souls III from Steam. Full instructions are in `ds3vr\README.txt`.

**Windows Defender:** some copies of Windows Defender flag the zip or `ds3vr-patcher.exe` as "Wacatac.B!ml". That is a machine-learning false positive for unsigned mods; it has been reported to Microsoft. If you trust the download, restore it from Protection history with "Allow on device".

**Runtimes:** tested on SteamVR, and on Virtual Desktop (VDXR) with a Meta Quest 3. PimaxXR should work but has not been fully tested yet; reports are welcome. **Quest owners:** use Virtual Desktop (VDXR); SteamVR over Quest Link has known problems.

**Credits:** NVIDIA DLSS by NVIDIA Corporation. Contrast-adaptive sharpening by AMD (FidelityFX CAS). geo-11 by davegl1234 and the HelixMod team; the Dark Souls 3 geo-11 fix by Helifax, updated by masterotaku.
